title: The Important letter from the office
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：important　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 important 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the director wrote of ① an important letter from the office in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② more important than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the important ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most important letter from the office anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1944 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too important to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the important ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an important visitor at the door, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as important as the visitor at the door they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was important or not, and he said so.

By 1957 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something important, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite important; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the important ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1960, in public, she wrote of another important letter from the office in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ more important than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most important visitor at the door in the whole theatre, she said in 1962, was the one she could never quite name; the important ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 重要（前置定语 an important letter from the office：1950 年导演在戏报里记下的那件重要的来函）
B. adj. 重要／显要（比较级 more important than：文中两处，一处比办公室的重要来函，一处比预想）
C. adj. 重要／显要（最高级 the most important：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 重要（表语 too important to do：母亲觉得它太重要，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 显要（前置定语 an important visitor at the door：叔叔把整件事称作一桩显要的来客）
F. adj. 显要（同级比较 as important as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩门口的显要来客相比）
G. adj. 显要（后置定语 something important：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 显要（受程度副词修饰 quite important：那位演员的评价）

items.q: an important letter from the office
the most important letter from the office anybody
an important visitor at the door
The most important visitor at the door in

answers.why: important 意为“重要”，1950 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件重要的来函”，此处作前置定语 an important letter from the office。
important 意为“重要”，此处用比较级 more important than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
important 意为“重要”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最重要的一件，故用最高级 the most important letter from the office。
important 意为“重要”，母亲认为这件东西“太重要了，谁也用不上”，too important to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
important 意为“显要”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩显要的来客”，此处作前置定语 an important visitor at the door。
important 意为“显要”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩门口的显要来客一样显要”，同级比较用 as important as。
important 意为“显要”，戏报上那半行字要的是“显要的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something important。
important 意为“显要”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当显要”，quite 修饰原级 important。
important 意为“显要”，1960 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要显要”，故用比较级 more important than。
important 意为“显要”，母亲 1962 年说的是“整个戏院里最显要的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most important visitor at the door。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1950 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件重要的来函。（an important letter from the office）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更重要。（more important than …）
母亲觉得它太重要，谁也用不上。（too important to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩显要的来客。（an important visitor at the door）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩门口的显要来客一样显要。（as important as …）
到了 1957 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件显要的东西。（something important）
answers: In 1950 the director wrote of an important letter from the office in the poster.
Everybody said it was more important than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too important to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an important visitor at the door.
He said nobody would call it as important as the visitor at the door they had once had.
By 1957 the poster asked for nothing but something important.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 important 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the director wrote of an important letter from the office in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most important letter from the office in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too important to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an important visitor at the door, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite important, and everybody laughed.
The important ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
